$comment: Cross-era: Bismarck belongs to the 1914 pack's prologue and to a future 1870 pack.

original.description: Bust portrait of Otto von Bismarck in a dark civilian frock coat with a high collar and dark cravat, arms folded, head turned to his right, with a small spray in the buttonhole.
original.archive: Internet Archive Book Images — the plate as reproduced in 'A history of mediæval and modern Europe for secondary schools' (1920); via Wikimedia Commons
original.licence: public domain — no known copyright restrictions (Internet Archive Book Images); the photographer died in 1910

colorization.author: Dave Tashner / Sandtable
colorization.method: AI-assisted colorization and upscale from the public-domain original, 2026
colorization.licence: Sandtable project licence; underlying photograph public domain
colorization.status: ok — label 'colorized (AI-assisted)'. Documented colours: black frock coat, white linen, grey hair. Caveat for the image review (sand-y0u.7): the Commons file is a crop of a halftone reproduction printed in a 1920 textbook, with its colour balance already adjusted by a Commons editor, so this colorization sits on a reproduction rather than an original print.

caption: Otto von Bismarck in 1890 — the year Wilhelm II dismissed him and let his treaty with Russia lapse. Colorized (AI-assisted) from a public-domain photograph.
credit: Original photograph: Jacques Pilartz, Cologne, 1890; Internet Archive Book Images via Wikimedia Commons; public domain. Colorization: Sandtable, AI-assisted, 2026.
notes: Provided by Dave 2026-08-23. Intended placement: the prologue's diplomatic origin — the alliance system that kept France and Russia apart, the dismissal of 1890, and the Franco-Russian alliance of 1894 that made the two-front problem the Schlieffen Plan was written to answer. used_by is deliberately empty until the prologue beats exist (sand-1l0.3), since the validator warns on ids that do not yet exist.
